title: 2 BOXES OF CARLTON WARE, ROYAL...
reason: Two boxes of about 25 decorative pieces with a Napoleon and Josephine vase pair, Royal Winton leaf ware, a Royal Doulton jug and an unmarked high-fired art-pottery style vase that could be much better than the rest; check the bases.
findings: Large mixed group of about 25 ceramic and metal pieces. Marks read: the base of the coffee cans reads 'Royal Doulton, English Translucent China, Clairmont, T.C.1033, Copyright Doulton & Co. Limited, Made in England' with the lion and crown (later 20th century backstamp); the base of the handled leaf server reads 'Royal Winton, Made in England, A' in script, with a metal disc where the chrome handle is fixed, and a second leaf dish in green and orange looks like a matching piece (its base is not shown). No Carlton Ware mark is visible on any piece, so the Carlton Ware claim is unconfirmed. Other pieces: a pair of two-handled shaded brown and red vases with transfer-printed portraits of Napoleon and Josephine (no base marks shown; Austrian or Bohemian style); a small Royal Doulton-style series ware jug with a village scene (base not shown); a green biscuit barrel with red and yellow poppies and a plated lid and swing handle; a brass urn with swags and ring handles; a teal vase with an enamel and gilt Japanese-style landscape (pagoda, mountain, gold moon) in the style of oriental ware from makers such as Carlton Ware but unmarked in the photo; a small cobalt vase with a pale blue run; a black conical vase with a gilt flower; a green ribbed mottled vase; a frilled pink and green jug; a twig-handled basket; a navy-banded white tureen and stand; and, in photo 8, an ovoid vase with a pale grey-green glaze and red-pink copper flushes that has the look of English high-fired art pottery (Ruskin or similar) or studio work, but with no base mark or signature shown that is only a possibility.
condition: No cracks or chips are visible in the photos, but bases, rims and handles are not shown for most pieces; plating on the biscuit barrel lid and mount is worn; the brass urn has an uneven patina; the tureen and cups look clean.
rescore_note: Mixed decorative ceramics of modest individual worth (Royal Doulton Clairmont cans, Royal Winton leaf server and dish, Napoleon and Josephine pair, Doulton-style jug, plated biscuit barrel, unmarked small vases); Carlton Ware is unconfirmed, and the unmarked pink-flushed grey-green vase is only a possible Ruskin (roughly one chance in four or five, base not shown), so it adds some upside but not enough to lift the lot out of the middle band; no price comparables checked because the web search limit was reached.
